newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Consumer, technology stocks seen top in Asia - guru.
newsitem.headline: Consumer, technology stocks seen top in Asia - guru.

text.p: Consumer and technology related stocks should top investor shopping lists in Asia, U.S. investment guru Peter Lynch said on Monday.
"My guess would be for consumer companies and technology-related firms," Lynch said when asked by reporters at a news conference which sectors he would target in Asia.

Lynch said spending on electronic consumables and products associated with a growing middle class would rise dramatically over the next decade as the region established itself as the driver of the global economy.
Consequently he saw earnings of regional companies involved in the consumer goods business -- from microwave oven makers to life insurers -- getting set to soar.
"When people get some money they want to buy things. It's human nature," Lynch said, explaining his forecast.
Lynch said he was "not an expert on Asia", but was confident that "emerging markets will do well over the next 20 to 30 years compared to the mature markets".

Lynch made his name on the strength of his commonsense approach to investment -- the "buy what you know" philosophy -- and built the Fidelity Magellan Fund into America's biggest mutual fund worth US$14 billion before retiring in 1990.
He said most people's approach to investing in the stock market was too short term and based on rumours, not knowledge.

"People will do research when they buy a microwave oven, but they'll hear a tip in the elevator and rush out and buy stock by sunset. If you have knowledge in an area, you should buy in that area. You shouldn't gamble," he said.
Playing for the long term was also key to investment success. A two to three year, profit-only outlook was too short, Lynch said.
"A stock won't pay you back in years two or three. It will be year five or six before it comes in," he said.
"You've got to ask yourself if you would like this company even if its stock fell. If you don't, don't buy it," Lynch added.
